question.text: Kolar Gold Fund (Cat II, 5-yr): Committed Capital INR 100 cr. Year 2 NAV pre-incentive = INR 105 cr. Year 2 HWM (prior year NAV pre-incentive) = INR 102 cr. Year 2 Reference Hurdle NAV (Year 2) = INR 121 cr. Incentive Fee rate 15%. Under the 'higher of HWM and Reference Hurdle' rule illustrated in the chapter, what Incentive Fee is the Manager eligible for in Year 2?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, incentive fees may be computed only when NAV pre-incentive exceeds the HIGHER of the Reference Hurdle NAV and the High-Water Mark; if the difference is negative, no incentive fee is payable. Applicable benchmark = max(INR 102 cr HWM, INR 121 cr Reference Hurdle) = INR 121 cr. NAV pre-incentive = INR 105 cr is BELOW INR 121 cr, so the incentive fee for Year 2 is INR 0. The Trap: Option A uses HWM only and ignores the higher Reference Hurdle benchmark. Option B uses the hurdle base but wrongly produces a positive figure when NAV is below the hurdle. Option D is mechanically unrelated to the source-backed formula. Note: HWM is a source-backed Cat I/II safeguard (generally applied at portfolio-company exit in deal-by-deal waterfalls). Only the daily-NAV crystallisation form of HWM sits outside the Cat I/II framework.
